aspects.says: A ChannelAdaptor runs one Receiver that reads continuously into <out> and one Sender that sends from <in>; application code only touches the queues.
basis: section:3.4 A Link Has One Reader That Never Stops: the ChannelAdaptor
aspects.reason: it is the shape of a deployment that only a running Q2 with a socket shows; the queue wiring is practised with QMUX in unit c4

aspects.says: The adaptor reconnects by itself after reconnect-delay and puts a new Date under <name>.ready for each connection.
basis: section:3.5 The Adaptor Reconnects and Announces the Link
aspects.reason: it needs Q2, a socket and real time; acting on a new ready object is practised in unit c11

aspects.says: The channel decides where a message ends and the packager what is inside it; a 2-byte binary length is an unsigned number, high byte first, and a wrong frame shows up as silence.
basis: section:3.1 The Channel Decides Where a Message Ends

aspects.says: A pool of raw channels mixes answers between borrowers and loses the answers that come after a read timeout, because the 2.1.7 channel closes its socket when the timeout fires.
basis: section:3.3.1 Spot the Problem: A Pool of Channels

aspects.says: A receiver reads exactly the announced length, across as many reads as it takes and one frame per call, and a stream that ends early is an error.
basis: section:3.2 One Read Is Not One Message

aspects.says: receive() returns the next frame, not your answer, never returns null, and its read timeout measures silence; silence and a closed connection are different exceptions.
basis: section:3.3 `receive()` Returns the Next Frame, Not Your Answer

aspects.says: A timeout attribute on <channel> and a <ready> element on the adaptor are ignored: the read timeout is the timeout property, the ready key is always <name>.ready.
basis: section:3.5.1 Two Settings That Do Nothing

aspects.says: GenericSSLSocketFactory accepts any certificate unless serverauth is true, then trusts the keystore and compares servername with the CN; passwords come from the environment.
basis: section:3.6 A TLS Channel Checks the Host Only When You Tell It To

aspects.says: A zero-length frame is a keep-alive: ASCIIChannel skips it, a binary channel needs expect-keep-alive or the adaptor drops the link.
basis: section:3.2 One Read Is Not One Message
